name: Adobe Portfolio
description: Adobe Portfolio is a Creative Cloud website builder for publishing responsive portfolio sites, project pages, custom domains, and creative work imported from selected Adobe services.
agentUseSummary: Adobe Portfolio cannot yet be connected through Relay. Adobe documents Portfolio as an Adobe ID and Creative Cloud subscription product operated through its web editor, with first-party Behance, Lightroom, Stock, Fonts, and Bridge workflows, but does not publish an Adobe Portfolio developer API, third-party application registration, least-privilege scopes, token lifecycle, or site-bound automation contract for Relay.

blocked.label: Connect Adobe Portfolio
blocked.description: Adobe does not publish an Adobe Portfolio application-registration, authorization, scope, token, revocation, endpoint, or least-privilege site-binding contract for a general Relay connector.

blocked.label: Read private Portfolio content
blocked.description: Draft pages, projects, images, media, site settings, contact data, password-protected content, domain configuration, and unpublished changes remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Edit or publish Portfolio content
blocked.description: Creating or changing sites, pages, projects, galleries, text, media, themes, integrations, domains, passwords, navigation, SEO, and live publication is blocked.

blocked.label: Administer Portfolio sites or accounts
blocked.description: Adobe identities, profiles, subscriptions, sites, collaborators, integrations, entitlements, domains, billing, and deletion cannot be administered through this provider.

blocked.label: Use private Adobe Portfolio interfaces
blocked.description: Browser automation, session cookies, Adobe ID credentials, private editor requests, scraping, undocumented endpoints, first-party Bridge integration reuse, and unrelated Adobe product APIs are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Adobe Portfolio action is enabled before Adobe publishes or contractually supplies a supported product API with exact site authority, least-privilege access, content fields, publication semantics, and lifecycle controls.

runtimeSupport.description: No Adobe Portfolio tools are mounted without a supported site-bound product API and approved publication contract.
No Adobe Portfolio tools are mounted without a supported site-bound product API and approved publication contract.

providerSetup.blocker: Adobe's current Portfolio documentation defines an Adobe ID and Creative Cloud subscription service operated through the Portfolio Editor. It documents selected first-party imports and publishing flows through Behance, Lightroom, Stock, Fonts, and Adobe Bridge, but no Portfolio-specific developer application, third-party authorization grant, scopes, endpoints, webhooks, token lifecycle, rate limits, site identifier contract, or automation terms. Adobe APIs for other products do not confer authority over Portfolio sites, and first-party Bridge or editor traffic cannot be repurposed as a Relay contract.
providerSetup.nextAction: Product, content, legal, privacy, security, and customer owners must obtain a current supported Adobe Portfolio integration contract from Adobe and select a representative entitled customer account. Freeze application ownership, exact Adobe profile and Portfolio site IDs, authentication and revocation, readable fields, draft and published states, password-protected and contact-data exclusions, allowed media sources, Behance and Lightroom boundaries, editing and publication approvals, domain and subscription exclusions, audit, rollback, deletion, rate, retention, and termination behavior before typed bounded wrappers and customer acceptance can be implemented.

evidence.supports: Adobe describes Portfolio as a Creative Cloud website builder with hosted content, up to five sites, customization, password protection, custom domains, and selected Adobe service imports.
Adobe's Portfolio integration documentation enumerates first-party Behance, Lightroom, Stock, and Fonts workflows and does not define a third-party application or product API contract.
Adobe documents publishing and updating through explicit actions in the Portfolio Editor and requires an active Creative Cloud subscription.
Adobe documents asset upload as a first-party Adobe Bridge workflow using an Adobe identity, followed by layout editing and publication in the Portfolio web editor.
Adobe's current general terms govern its websites, web applications, Creative Cloud services, software, accounts, content, conduct, and restrictions relevant to any future supported integration.
